findings.title: Shard path interpolates each target twice, once here and again in runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target, and splitQueriesByStreamShard then passes each sub-request (whose expr already has the shard selector inserted) into runSplitQuery. runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts (line 299) calls applyTemplateVariables again on those targets. The expression is interpolated twice. For values containing '$', regex metacharacters, or values that Loki's formatter escapes, a second pass can change or corrupt the query. The second pass is not needed for correctness, and the two call sites should not both interpolate.

findings.title: $__range guard in querySupportsSplitting now sees interpolated expressions
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting (line 287) checks isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to keep queries using $__range out of splitting, and the comment explains that the variable must stay un-interpolated. Interpolation now runs before partitioning (here, before querySupportsSplitting is called), so if applyTemplateVariables resolves $__range to a concrete range, the guard no longer matches and such queries get split, which the comment says breaks them. The guard should be evaluated on the raw expression, or the PR should confirm that $__range is not resolved by applyTemplateVariables.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation
findings.body: The filter `query.expr` (line 298) is applied before applyTemplateVariables (line 299). A query whose expr is a template variable that interpolates to an empty string is not dropped and is sent to the backend as an empty query. The emptiness check should happen after interpolation, as the stated goal of this PR is to interpolate first.

findings.title: Test asserts an exact applyTemplateVariables call count that couples it to internals
findings.body: The assertion `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` depends on how many times interpolation happens across the top-level call and each nested runSplitQuery sub-request. It does not check the behavior the test name describes (interpolated before running), and it will break on any refactor that changes the number of passes, including the double-interpolation fix. It also hides the double-interpolation problem, since the count of 5 is the symptom of it.
